blocks.text: Paris, France—War, economic pressure, budget strain — United Nations (UN) biodiversity chief Astrid Schomaker is under no illusions that the upcoming UN nature summit (COP17) is taking place “in some kind of geopolitical vacuum”. “I don’t want to be naive,” said Schomaker of the headwinds surrounding the biennial negotiations on protecting the natural world that start on October 19 in Yerevan, Armenia. “Clearly, geopolitics enter also the debate on biodiversity,” the executive secretary of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) told AFP in English from Montreal.
